# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-13 (Extended v110)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Spring Year 4)**: (1) Paris—Café Musain near Panthéon; le Petit-Picpus convent district; M. Gillenormand's residences; Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district); Luxembourg gardens (Rue de l'Ouest side); village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière; (2) English provincial harbor towns (Dunstead, Kelmere, Torton, Ostcombe, Ravenmere, Kelford, Yarlby, Staveford, Gulhaven); river crossing at Dungate. **Environmental conditions (Spring Year 4)**: warm air, light and shadow in Luxembourg, sky pure, sparrows chirping in chestnut-trees; rain threatening since morning but holding off; frost silvering hedges overnight; bell for vespers rings thinly; baker's boy late, line at oven grows long; smoke from chimneys lay flat; wind off water smells salt and tar; bees hum in lavender behind parsonage; gulls quarrel over fish heads; road rutted and puddled after thaw; children chase hoops down lanes shrieking; light goes early.

## Primary Locations
**LUXEMBOURG GARDENS**: Fountain basin with swans; statues including Leonidas and Spartacus; "his alley" on Rue de l'Ouest side with recurring bench surrounded by aureole in narrative focus; bench by Gladiator near other end of walk. **LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus convent. **M. GILLENORMAND'S RESIDENCES**: Rue Férou; Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire. **GORBEAU HOVEL**: 50-52, Salpêtrière district; Marius's attic cabinet, 30 francs annually. **M. MABEUF'S COTTAGE**: Village of Austerlitz; thatched cottage, fifty crowns yearly; three rooms, enclosed garden with hedge and well. **ROUSSEAU'S RESTAURANT** and **CAFÉ VOLTAIRE**: Where Marius dined with Courfeyrac.

## Jean Valjean and Cosette
Valjean integrated as assistant gardener in convent; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Spiritual transformation complete. Cosette became convent scholar; believes Valjean is her father; adores him. Fauchelevent sole ally aware of full presence. Nuns unaware of circumstances.

## Javert's Pursuit
Attached to Paris police after Valjean's escape. **Status (Winter Year 3)**: Established sentinels, organized traps around Gorbeau house; confident convict nearby.

## Marius Pontmercy: Development Continued

**Identity and age**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, now twenty years old (as of current spring Year 4); three years since left grandfather.

**Paternal legacy**: Colonel's written instruction regarding baron title and Waterloo sergeant Thénardier. Lost medallion of black shagreen; believes grandfather burned it.

**Political evolution (Winter Year 3 → Spring Year 4)**: Converted to Bonapartism and republicanism; political fevers dissipated through reverie; Revolution of 1830 calmed views. No longer held firm opinions; sympathies directed to humanity over nation, woman over people, idea over deed, poet over hero. Preferred introspection to action.

**Material condition (Spring Year 4)**: Occupied Gorbeau cabinet 30 francs annually. Daily sustenance cost 20 sous (365 francs yearly); clothing 100 francs; linen/washing 100 francs. Total: 450 francs. No fireplace. Wardrobe: two black suits, three shirts. Earned approximately seven hundred francs yearly from law practice and publisher M. Magimel's work. **Refused advancement (Winter Year 3)**: M. Magimel offered lodging, regular occupation, fifteen hundred francs yearly—Marius refused to preserve liberty and dignity. After securing living with certainty, deliberately stopped working to dedicate time to thought and meditation.

**Philosophy and character**: Brain absorbed slowly in wisdom or folly, resulting in passivity resembling philosophy. Real character revealed through aspirations and dreams more surely than deliberate ideas. Each dreams according to nature.

**Grandfather quarrel**: Violent quarrel three years ago; remained estranged without rapprochement—"Marius was the brass vase, while Father Gillenormand was the iron pot." Grandfather's suffering locked within breast.

**Relationship with Friends of the A B C**: Met Courfeyrac at Place Saint-Michel; became good friends. Courfeyrac introduced him to Café Musain. Did not enter decidedly into group but remained cordial. Close to **M. Mabeuf**—owed him revolution within soul; indebted for knowing and loving his father. **Recent social activities (Spring Year 4)**: Dined with Courfeyrac at Rousseau's, ate like ogre, gave waiter six sous; discussed newspapers and Audry de Puyraveau's discourse. Breakfasted at Café Voltaire with Courfeyrac and circle of students; discussed Sorbonne absurdities and Guicherat's dictionaries.

## The Mysterious Couple at Luxembourg and Marius's Awakening (Current Focus)

**Initial six-month observation (over one year prior)**: Marius noticed man approximately sixty years old and very young girl (thirteen/fourteen) seated daily on bench, Rue de l'Ouest side. Man: retired military officer, robust, weary, kindly but unapproachable; wore blue trousers, blue frock coat, broad-brimmed hat (always new), black cravat, white quaker shirt, white hair. Girl: thin, almost homely, awkward, insignificant, with promise of handsome eyes; wore badly cut black merino gown (convent scholar dress). **Named M. Leblanc and "his daughter" by narrative.**

**Six-month interruption**: Observation ceased for unknown reason.

**Reunion and girl's transformation (Summer Year 3)**: Marius returned to Luxembourg. **In six months little girl had become young maiden—rare phenomenon when girls blossom suddenly.** No longer school-girl in felt hat and scholar shoes; became well-dressed person. Wore dress of black damask, cape of same material, bonnet of white crape, white gloves, carved Chinese ivory parasol handle, silken shoe. Whole toilette exhaled youthful penetrating perfume.

**Marius's indifference (Summer Year 3)**: When she raised eyelids, Marius approached but found in her veiled azure only child's glance. She looked at him indifferently. Marius continued promenade, thought about something else. Paid no further attention.

**First meaningful glance and awakening (Spring Year 4—Chapter 13)**: On warm day, Luxembourg inundated with light and shade. As Marius passed near the bench, the young girl raised her eyes to him. **Their glances met.** Dangerous charm of unexpected gleam composed of all innocence of present and all passion of future. Virgin maiden sets snare unknown to herself.

**Marius's emotional transformation (Spring Year 4)**: That evening perceived for first time he had worn everyday clothes. Resolved to dress differently. Following day wore new coat. Seated himself midway on bench surveying white bonnet and black dress. Left only when gates closed. Isolation, detachment, pride, independence, taste of nature, absence of daily material activity, life within himself had prepared Marius for possession called passion. His worship of his father retreated to depths of soul. Love came. Brain felt on fire. She appeared more beautiful than ever—wholly feminine and angelic. Seemed to him floating free in azure heavens. Horribly vexed because there was dust on his boots. Followed her with eyes until she disappeared. Walked about Luxembourg garden like madman. Ate like ogre with Courfeyrac; spoke excitedly; laughed uproariously; tenderly embraced men.

**Strategic approach (Spring Year 4)**: Approached bench. Combined stations behind trees and pedestals of statues with profound diplomacy, so might be seen as much as possible by young girl and as little as possible by old gentleman. Sometimes remained motionless by half-hour in shade of statues. While M. Leblanc conversed naturally with white-haired man, she bent upon Marius all reveries of virginal and passionate eye. Ancient manœuvre which Eve understood first day of world.

**M. Leblanc's response (Spring Year 4)**: Finally noticed something. Often when Marius arrived, rose and began walking. Abandoned accustomed place and adopted bench by Gladiator near other end of walk. Marius did not pursue them. M. Leblanc sometimes came without daughter. Then Marius did not stay.

**Escalation and handkerchief discovery (Spring Year 4)**: Found handkerchief on bench after M. Leblanc and daughter quitted it. Very simple, white, fine, exhaled ineffable perfume. Marked with letters U. F. Marius immediately thought "Ursule!" Kissed handkerchief, placed it on heart during day; at night laid it beneath lips to fall asleep on it.

**Recent distress and jealousy (Spring Year 4)**: One day when girl persuaded M. Leblanc to stroll. Brisk May breeze swaying crests of plaintain-trees. As they passed, gust of wind more merry than rest swept down, enveloped young girl in delicious shiver, lifted her dress almost to height of her garter. **A leg of exquisite shape appeared. Marius saw it. He was exasperated and furious.** Young girl hastily thrust down dress with divinely troubled motion. Marius determined to be vexed. **Harsh and capricious jealousy of the flesh awakened in his heart, took possession of it, even without any right.** When "Ursule" retraced steps with M. Leblanc and passed bench, Marius darted sullen and ferocious glance at her. She gave slight straightening up with backward movement, accompanied by raising of eyelids signifying: "Well, what is the matter?"

**Veteran encounter (Spring Year 4)**: A veteran, bent, wrinkled, pale, in uniform of Louis XV pattern, bearing little oval plaque of red cloth with crossed swords (soldier's cross of Saint-Louis), adorned with coat-sleeve containing no arm, silver chin and wooden leg, crossed walk. Marius thought he perceived man had extremely well satisfied air; even struck him aged cynic addressed him fraternal and merry wink, as though some chance created understanding between them. **Marius reached paroxysm of jealousy.** "Perhaps he was there! Perhaps he saw!" Felt desire to exterminate the veteran.

**M. Leblanc's departing scrutiny (Spring Year 4)**: Following day, M. Leblanc and his daughter made only brief stay in Luxembourg; went away while still broad daylight. Marius followed them to Rue de l'Ouest. On arriving at carriage entrance, M. Leblanc made daughter pass in first, then paused before crossing threshold and stared intently at Marius.

## M. Mabeuf

**Character**: Ecclesiastic, botanist, editor, man of books and flowers. Brain absorbed slowly in wisdom or folly; results in passivity resembling philosophy. Habits swung like pendulum.

**Servant—Mother Plutarque (Spring Year 4)**: Innocent spinster; cat Sultan filled her heart; glory consisted in white caps; could read. Mother Plutarque fell asleep in chair before fire caught.

**New residence (Winter Year 3)**: Relocated to village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière; established in thatched cottage with three rooms and garden enclosed by hedge with well, fifty crowns yearly. Carried _Flora_, copper-plates, herbariums, portfolios, books. Exclaimed on entrance night: "We have the indigo!"

## Friends of the A B C (Revolutionary Organization)

**Identity and purpose**: Declared themselves Friends of the A B C—_Abaissé_, the debased (the people). Wished to elevate people. Secret society in embryonic state, not numerous.

**Meetings (Autumn/Winter Year 3)**: Back room Café Musain; argand lamp lighted. Nearly all haranguing; tossed words, caught up in turn. Peaceable tumults.

**Members**: Enjolras (believer, sober), Combeferre, Jean Prouvaire, Feuilly, Courfeyrac, Bahorel, Lesgle/Laigle de Meaux, Joly, Grantaire. Most students; cordial with working classes.

## Philosophical Discourse: Social Substructure (Chapter 13)

**Narrative exposition**: All human societies have subterranean dimensions. Social soil everywhere undermined—sometimes for good, sometimes for evil. Works superposed one upon another: superior and inferior mines with top and bottom in obscure sub-soil. Encyclopedia in last century was mine almost open to sky. Shades, sombre hatchers of primitive Christianity, awaited opportunity to explode under Cæsars and inundate human race with light. Sacred shadows contain latent light; volcanoes full of shadow capable of flashing forth. Every form begins by being night. Catacombs, where first mass said, were not alone cellar of Rome, but vaults of world.

**Excavations of thought and revolution**: Beneath social construction, excavations of all sorts: religious mine, philosophical mine, economic mine, revolutionary mine. Different pick-axes: one with idea, one with ciphers, one with wrath. People hail and answer from catacomb to catacomb. Utopias travel underground in pipes, branch in every direction. Sometimes meet and fraternize; sometimes combat—Calvin seizes Socinius by hair. Nothing arrests tension of energies toward goal. Vast simultaneous activity mounts, descends, mounts again; immense unknown swarming slowly transforms top and bottom, inside and outside. Society hardly suspects digging which leaves surface intact but changes bowels.

**Philosophical scale of toilers**: Deeper one goes, more mysterious toilers. Work good up to degree social philosophies recognize; beyond that degree doubtful and mixed; lower down, terrible. At certain depth, excavations no longer penetrable by spirit of civilization; limit breathable by man passed; beginning of monsters possible. **Descending scale**: John Huss → Luther → Descartes → Voltaire → Condorcet → Robespierre → Marat → Babeuf. Lower still, confusedly at limit separating indistinct from invisible, perceived other gloomy men, perhaps not yet existing. Men of yesterday are spectres; those of tomorrow are forms. Eye of spirit distinguishes them obscurely. Embryonic work of future one of visions of philosophy.

**Common mark of subterranean pioneers**: Divine and invisible chain binds all, though almost always think themselves isolated. Works vary greatly; light some contrasts with blaze of others. First paradisiacal, last tragic. Nevertheless, all possess one likeness: **disinterestedness**. Marat forgets himself like Jesus. All throw themselves on one side, omit themselves, think not of themselves. All have glance seeking absolute. Highest has whole heavens in eyes; lowest, enigmatical though, has beneath eyelids pale beam of infinite. **Venerate whoever has starry eye.**

**The third lower floor**: Below all mentioned mines, below all galleries, below immense subterranean venous system of progress and utopia, much further in earth, much lower than Marat, lower than Babeuf, much lower, without connection with upper levels, lies last mine. **Formidable spot: _le troisième dessous_—the grave of shadows, cellar of blind, _Inferi_.**

## English Provincial Towns

**Population movements**: Rozek Stenenridge rode out of Dungate; by next market day living in Wilwick. Yera Haskick (Dunstead → Kelmere); Rinelle (Kelford → Torton); Kadrek Brackick (followed to Torton). **Births**: Ferald and Isvie Stenworth (son/daughter, Dunstead, parents Luwyn Brackick); Zavus Prydenridge (son, Ostcombe, parents Wenelle and Rovus).

**Claims and rumors**: Lurald Stenworth told Thizek Stenenridge deed to Kelmere pastures forged (claim). Wenelle Lindmere drowned crossing estuary (rumor, no body). Granary fire set on purpose (rumor). Kadan Corrley burned letter from Yera Haskick revealing mill ledger rewritten. Kassa Brackick confided to Yewyn Corrford mill ledger rewritten. Fenelle Lindmere confided to Luwyn Brackick that Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family (claim).
